analysis: All changes are in test files (EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift, new EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift) plus a doc-comment edit in the SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift fixture. There is no production code, no wire protocol change, no key handling, and no attestation or authorization change in this batch. The tests exercise EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry and productionSchedulerConfig. They assert that the wide 2048-token plain chunk replaces the former 2048 solo stripe for GPT-OSS, Gemma 4 and dense Qwen. The paged pool ring size, max(chunk, stripe), stays unchanged. Bidirectional media keeps a 512 ceiling. Malformed env overrides fall back to the SDK geometry, and explicit chunk/budget overrides are covered including Int.max saturation. Relevant threat areas are TB-007 (inference engine) and T-041 (prefix cache). The tests set the prefix cache to disabled or ephemeral-test roots using temp directories and an in-memory KEK, with no real key material. They also confirm that the SSD checkpoint layout, kill switches and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate behave as the threat model describes, and nothing weakens them. The production change that these tests accompany (EngineV2Factory prefill geometry) is not in the supplied units. Integration should check whether that change affects T-010 (cancellation latency with wider chunks), DoS/availability from larger prefill chunks, and the memory bounds of the paged pool. The tests pin pool sizing as unchanged, which is reassuring but cannot be verified against the unseen source. No concrete regression is identified here.
